### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [X] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version

### Module(s)

mini.starter

### Description

I will be frank, this bug is specific to [my config](https://github.com/alex35mil/dotfiles/tree/158026643f2bc9306ca67a04a4783364abf5c9b8/home/.config/nvim). I can't reproduce it in basic setup, and I spent a few hours this weekend to debug it but still have no clue where does it come from.

Anyway, here are the details. In my LazyVim-based config, when `mini.starter` is active and I add a new plugin, lazy installs the plugin, but then `mini.starter` crashes with the following error:

```
Error detected while processing VimEnter Autocommands for "*"..VimEnter Autocommands for "*":
Error executing lua callback: ....local/share/nvim/lazy/mini.starter/lua/mini/starter.lua:1479: bad argument #1 to 'len' (string expected, got nil)
stack traceback:
	[builtin:len]: in function 'len'
	....local/share/nvim/lazy/mini.starter/lua/mini/starter.lua:1479: in function 'is_something_shown'
	....local/share/nvim/lazy/mini.starter/lua/mini/starter.lua:1060: in function <....local/share/nvim/lazy/mini.starter/lua/mini/starter.lua:1059>
	[C]: in function 'nvim_exec_autocmds'
	...hare/nvim/lazy/lazy.nvim/lua/lazy/core/handler/event.lua:161: in function <...hare/nvim/lazy/lazy.nvim/lua/lazy/core/handler/event.lua:160>
	[C]: in function 'xpcall'
	.../.local/share/nvim/lazy/lazy.nvim/lua/lazy/core/util.lua:135: in function 'try'
	...hare/nvim/lazy/lazy.nvim/lua/lazy/core/handler/event.lua:160: in function '_trigger'
	...hare/nvim/lazy/lazy.nvim/lua/lazy/core/handler/event.lua:143: in function 'trigger'
	...hare/nvim/lazy/lazy.nvim/lua/lazy/core/handler/event.lua:89: in function <...hare/nvim/lazy/lazy.nvim/lua/lazy/core/handler/event.lua:72>
```

Somehow, [`first_line` here](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.starter/blob/3e0af795938ee800846708bed92fbe4e8583141a/lua/mini/starter.lua#L1479) is `nil`.

And AFAICT this is [the code](https://github.com/LazyVim/LazyVim/blob/a1c3ec4cd43fe61e3b614237a46ac92771191c81/lua/lazyvim/plugins/extras/ui/mini-starter.lua#L50-L59) that leads to the crash:

```lua
    -- close Lazy and re-open when starter is ready
    if vim.o.filetype == "lazy" then
      vim.cmd.close()
      vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("User", {
        pattern = "MiniStarterOpened",
        callback = function()
          require("lazy").show()
        end,
      })
    end
```

I wasn't able to figure out in which circumstances `vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0, 0, 1, true)[1]` can produce `nil` there, but maybe it's worth handling and perhaps you have a clue.

### Neovim version

0.10.1

### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone [my config](https://github.com/alex35mil/dotfiles/tree/158026643f2bc9306ca67a04a4783364abf5c9b8/home/.config/nvim).
2. Add any new plugin to the `lua/plugins`.
3. Restart Neovim.
4. Lazy should install the added plugin, but then the starter should crash with the mentioned error.


### Expected behavior

Starter doesn't crash after plugin install.

### Actual behavior

Starter crashes with the mentioned error.

comment_data.body:
> I will be frank, this bug is specific to [my config](https://github.com/alex35mil/dotfiles/tree/158026643f2bc9306ca67a04a4783364abf5c9b8/home/.config/nvim). I can't reproduce it in basic setup, and I spent a few hours this weekend to debug it but still have no clue where does it come from.

Then the proper route would have been not creating an issue, but a [question in Discussions](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/discussions/categories/q-a).

------

I tried reproducing (all the way with cloning config and adding new plugin), but was not able to. All I can see is that 'mini.starter' text is not aligned, but no errors.

The suspiciously `nil` first line should never happen. The only case when `vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0, 0, 1, true)` can return empty array is for unloaded buffers, but current buffer can never be unloaded.

So my guess is that something does **very** bad monkey-patching in your setup. Maybe conflict with previous stage of your config, as you moved to LazyVim 2 days ago. Maybe try cleaning all the standard paths (like '~/.local/share/nvim' and '~/.local/state/nvim') as it might contain some conflicting code.

It turned out to be specific to my config _and_ Neovide, but I didn’t figure out why it happens. I ended up disabling auto-installation and conditionally adding starter entry if there’s anything to install.

title: mini.starter: starter screen crashes after lazy installs a new plugin
